title: SLA-aware profile stitcher for onboarding: guided dataset + runner mappings
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a harness component that stitches together dataset slices, prompt variants, and evaluator runner configurations to produce SLA-aware performance profiles for newly onboarded model versions. The stitcher should prioritize generating targeted profiles that exercise tail latency, throughput under burst, and accuracy slices tied to customer SLAs, producing artifacts compatible with the profile publisher pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: New 'profile-stitcher' module generates a JSON profile bundle containing dataset references, prompt permutations, per-scenario expected metrics and runner hints
Profiles include explicit SLA tags (latency_p99_ms, throughput_target_rps, quality_threshold) and runner_affinity suggestions (low-latency, high-throughput, quantized)
Generated profiles are consumable by the existing profile validator and the publishing pipeline without transformation
Automated smoke eval runs (sampled subset) produce stable metrics within ±15% of expected for two internal test models
Documentation and example config added to the harness repo and linked in onboarding playbook
technical_notes: Stitcher will take inputs: model metadata (arch, params, quantization options), onboarding checklist (SLA targets), workload fingerprint (traffic shape), and dataset catalog pointers.

Algorithm: assign scenario weights via SLA-driven heuristics -> select dataset slices using weighted stratified sampling -> produce prompt variants using existing prompt-transform library -> attach runner hints using simple cost-latency model and a scoring function that favors compatible kernels/quantization profiles.

Output schema is a flat JSON array of scenarios; each scenario is represented as an id string, dataset path string, prompt_template string, expected_metrics string (encoded as key:value pairs), runner_hint string (one of: low-latency, high-throughput, fallback-quantized).
We intentionally avoid complex ML-based selection in v1 to keep onboarding deterministic and debuggable.
Integrations: profile validator (ENG-73321), profile publisher (ENG-92784), benchmark harness (ENG-71234).
progress_updates: 2026-02-25: Kickoff meeting with PM and Design; aligned on SLA tag surface. Decided v1 will use heuristics rather than learned selectors.

2026-03-04: Implemented prototype stitcher that emits 10 scenarios for sample model. Ran the smoke eval harness locally; observed p99 estimates were optimistic for transformer-xl variants.
2026-03-07: Pulled kernel compatibility matrix into scoring function to avoid suggesting quantized runners for unsupported ops. Updated unit tests.
2026-03-10: Integration PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/harness/pull/2147. Requesting design review on prompt-variant templates (link below).
notes_for_reviewers: Pay attention to the runner_hint taxonomy; we added 'fallback-quantized' to support graceful degradation paths.
We need agreement on acceptable metric tolerances for auto-generated profiles (currently ±15%).
For QA: run smoke evals with two internal models (base-3B and base-70B-quant) and verify runner hints are sensible.
